unsupported_claims: LINE(2nd) beats LINE(1st) on social network classification (e.g., Flickr and YouTube)
For these datasets, neighborhood-overlap information carries more useful signal than direct adjacency
Second-order proximity explanation: shared-neighbor similarity explains LINE(2nd)'s advantage on social networks
rationale: The answer accepts the false premise and asserts that LINE(2nd) beats LINE(1st) on social networks (Flickr, YouTube). The paper reports the opposite: LINE(1st) is slightly better, because first-order proximity (strong ties) matters more and sparsity makes second-order proximity inaccurate. Only the closing remark that the two proximities are complementary is supported.
